Incorporating SLOOS insights tilts the outlook more negative than the FSR-only read. While the March 15, 2020 FOMC actions provided aggressive easing and liquidity backstops, the April 2020 SLOOS indicates a rapid tightening in the credit channel: banks tightened standards and other terms across C&I and CRE (including construction and land development), raised credit score thresholds, cut credit limits, and reported weaker demand in several segments. Banks also expected further tightening, reduced risk tolerance, and deterioration in loan performance and collateral values (including HELOCs), with only pockets of unchanged demand (e.g., some consumer categories). These credit supply headwinds and deteriorating expectations amplify downside macro risks despite policy support. Net sentiment shifts more negative.
